([[Radnor, Pennsylvania]]) | college = [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels men's basketball|UNLV]] (2015–2016) | draft_year = 2016 | career_start = 2016 | years1 = {{nbay|2016|start}}–{{nbay|2017|start}} | team1 = [[Phoenix Suns]] | years2 = [[2016–17 NBA Development League season|2016–2017]] | team2 = →[[Motor City Cruise|Northern Arizona Suns]] | years4 = {{nbay|2017|start}}–{{nbay|2019|end}} | team4 = [[Miami Heat]] | years5 = [[2017–18 NBA G League season|2017–2018]] | team5 = →[[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] | years6 = {{nbay|2020|full=y}} | team6 = [[Portland Trail Blazers]] | years7 = {{nbay|2021|start}}–{{nbay|2022|end}} | team7 = [[Chicago Bulls]] | years8 = {{nbay|2023|full=y}} | team8 = [[Dallas Mavericks]] | years9 = {{nbay|2024|start}}–present | team9 = [[Los Angeles Clippers]] | highlights = * [[NBA Slam Dunk Contest]] champion ([[2020 NBA All-Star Game|2020]]) * [[Mr. and Miss Pennsylvania Basketball|Mr. Pennsylvania Basketball]] (2015) }} '''Derrick Labrent Jones Jr.''' (born February 15, 1997) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels men's basketball|UNLV Runnin' Rebels]]. He is nicknamed "'''Airplane Mode'''" because of his [[Slam dunk|dunking]] ability.{{cite web |last=Fernandez |first=Andre |date=January 8, 2020 |title=Heat’s Derrick Jones Jr.’s dunks have been compared to Dominique Wilkins’, but ‘I jump higher,’ he says |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1511413/2020/01/08/heats-derrick-jones-jr-s-dunks-have-been-compared-to-dominique-wilkins-but-i-jump-higher-he-says/ |access-date=December 21, 2023 |work=The Athletic}}{{cite web|first=Jeremy|last=Cluff|title=Airplane Mode: The Suns' Derrick Jones Jr. can dunk|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/heat-index/2017/02/03/airplane-mode-suns-derrick-jones-jr-can-dunk/97455834/|website=AZCentral.com|date=February 17, 2017|access-date=May 14, 2024}} ==High school career== As a senior at [[Archbishop John Carroll High School]] in 2014–15, he was named the Southeastern Pennsylvania Player of the Year, the Delaware County Player of the Year, was the PIAA Triple-A Player of the Year, and was selected first-team All-Catholic League. Under coach Paul Romanczuk, Archbishop Carroll went 23–7 overall in 2014–15, including a 12–3 mark in conference play. In the semifinals of the state tournament, he recorded 30 points, 18 rebounds and five blocked shots while his rival Jonah Pournazarian scored 44. For the season, he averaged 19.2 points, 10.1 rebounds and 2.3 blocks per game. During his high school career, he scored 1,645 points, collected 1,029 rebounds and blocked 268 shots, finishing as the highest scorer in school history.{{cite web|url= https://unlvrebels.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/derrick-jr-/5212|title=Derrick Jones Jr. Bio|work=UNLVRebels.com|access-date=September 25, 2016}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2015}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Derrick Jones | position = [[Small forward|SF]] | hometown = [[Philadelphia, Pennsylvania]] | highschool = [[Archbishop John Carroll High School|Archbishop John Carroll]] | feet = 6 | inches = 6 | weight = 180 | 40 = | commitdate = November 13, 2014 | scout stars = 4 | rivals stars = 4 | 247 stars = 4 | espn stars = 4 | bball = yes }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | rivals ref title = https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/5865 | scout ref title = http://www.scout.com/player/169636-derrick-jones?s=75 | espn ref title = http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/166853/derrick-jones | rivals overall = 49 | scout overall = 84 | espn overall = 30 }} ==College career== Jones joined the [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels men's basketball|UNLV Runnin' Rebels]] for his freshman season in the 2015–16 NCAA season. Prior to the start of the season, the NCAA Eligibility Center requested that the ACT investigate test scores recorded by Jones from a particular testing site in Baltimore, Maryland.{{cite web|first=Paul|last=Coro|title=Derrick Jones Jr. takes unexpected NBA detour to Suns|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2016/10/11/derrick-jones-jr-takes-unexpected-nba-detour-suns/91919078/|work=AZentral.com|date=October 11, 2016|access-date=October 11, 2016}} Despite this, Jones was cleared by the NCAA prior to UNLV's first game against [[2015–16 Cal Poly Mustangs men's basketball team|Cal Poly]] in November.{{cite web|first=Mike|last=DeCourcy|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/news/derrick-jones-unlv-test-scores-ineligible-ncaa-investigation/sqrnd6ajbnp0z5vd52u591vh|title=NCAA disqualifies Derrick Jones over test scores; attorney blasts timeline, motivation|work=SportingNews.com|date=March 2, 2016|access-date=September 25, 2016}} Jones was the Runnin' Rebels' second-leading scorer in 2015–16. He averaged 11.5 points on 58.9 percent shooting and 4.5 rebounds in 30 games. Jones recorded four double-doubles during the season, including a career-high 26 points to go with 10 rebounds against [[Chaminade Silverswords|Chaminade]] at the [[Maui Invitational Tournament]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/phoenix-suns-sign-four-players-ahead-training-camp|title=Phoenix Suns Sign Four Players ahead of Training Camp|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=September 25, 2016|access-date=September 25, 2016}} On February 29, 2016, UNLV was notified by the ACT testing service that Jones' score had been cancelled. As a result, Jones was deemed ineligible to compete under NCAA rules and was forced to sit out the remaining three games of UNLV's season.{{cite web|first=Sam|last=Vecenie|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/unlvs-derrick-jones-now-ineligible-due-to-act-being-thrown-out/|title=UNLV's Derrick Jones now ineligible due to ACT being thrown out|work=CBSSports.com|date=March 2, 2016|access-date=September 25, 2016}} ==Professional career== ===Phoenix Suns (2016–2017)=== On April 7, 2016, Jones declared for the [[2016 NBA draft]], but left open the possibility of returning to UNLV or going to another college program by not hiring an agent.{{cite web|first=Mark|last=Anderson|url=https://www.reviewjournal.com/sports/unlv-rebels/basketball/unlv-s-derrick-jones-jr-declares-nba-draft|title=UNLV's Derrick Jones Jr. declares for NBA Draft|work=ReviewJournal.com|date=April 7, 2016|access-date=September 25, 2016}} Later that month, Jones hired an agent and remained in the draft.{{cite web|first=Dan|last=Stack|url=http://www.todaysu.com/u-news/unlv-forward-derrick-jones-jr-hires-agent-will-stay-nba-draft/|title=UNLV F Derrick Jones Jr. hires agent & will stay in NBA draft|work=TodaySU.com|date=April 18, 2016|access-date=September 25, 2016}} Jones ultimately went undrafted in the 2016 draft, and subsequently joined the [[Sacramento Kings]] for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|first=Dan|last=Lovi|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/blog/get-know-2016-kings-summer-league-team/|title=Get to Know: 2016 Kings Summer League Team|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=July 8, 2016|access-date=September 25, 2016}} However, due to a groin injury, he was unable to play for the Kings during the tournament.{{cite web|url=https://www.reviewjournal.com/sports/basketball/nba-summer-league/nba-summer-league-day-6-blog-unlv-s-derrick-jones-sidelined|title=NBA Summer League Day 6 blog: UNLV's Derrick Jones sidelined by groin injury|work=ReviewJournal.com|date=July 13, 2016|access-date=September 25, 2016}} On September 25, 2016, Jones signed with the [[Phoenix Suns]] for training camp. Jones secured an opening-night roster spot after impressing the Suns during training camp and preseason.{{cite web|title=Phoenix Suns Waive Archie Goodwin, Reduce Roster to 15|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/phoenix-suns-waive-archie-goodwin-reduce-roster-15|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=October 24, 2016|access-date=November 6, 2016}}{{cite web|first=Kevin|last=Zimmerman|url=https://arizonasports.com/story/875311/suns-release-archie-goodwin/|title=Suns release guard Archie Goodwin, retain Jenkins and Jones Jr.|work=ArizonaSports.com|date=October 24, 2016|access-date=October 24, 2016}} He made his NBA debut in his home state against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] on November 19, 2016,{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/j/jonesde02/gamelog/2017/|title=Derrick Jones 2016–17 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=November 20, 2016}} and recorded his first field goal in the NBA to finish with three points in three minutes against the [[San Antonio Spurs]] on December 15, 2016.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400899829|title=Spurs vs. Suns – Box Score|publisher=ESPN|date=December 15, 2016|access-date=December 15, 2016}} Despite spending much of the 2016–17 season in the [[NBA Development League]] with the [[Northern Arizona Suns]],{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/|title=All-Time NBA Assignments|publisher=National Basketball Association|access-date=December 7, 2017}} Jones was selected to compete in the [[NBA Slam Dunk Contest]].{{cite web|last=Kotloff|first=Brian|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/derrick-jones-jr-nba-dunk-contest-dleague/|title=Meet Derrick Jones Jr., the NBA D-Leaguer in the NBA Dunk Contest|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=February 2, 2017|access-date=February 2, 2017|archive-date=June 9, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170609125706/http://dleague.nba.com/news/derrick-jones-jr-nba-dunk-contest-dleague/|url-status=dead}} He went on to make it through to the final round of the Slam Dunk Contest, where he ultimately lost to [[Glenn Robinson III]]. On February 28, 2017, he scored eight points in a 130–112 loss to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. Two days later, he had another eight-point effort in a 123–103 win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]]. On March 11, 2017, in a 100–98 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]], Jones made his first start, logging two points, a season-high seven rebounds, and one assist. On March 28, 2017, he had his first double-digit scoring game of his career, scoring 13 points in a 95–91 loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400900501|title=Suns vs. Hawks|publisher=ESPN|date=March 28, 2017|access-date=March 28, 2017}} On April 9, 2017, he scored a career-high 15 points in a 124–111 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900577|title=Warren, Booker lead Suns past Mavericks, 124–111|publisher=ESPN|date=April 9, 2017|access-date=April 9, 2017}} In July 2017, Jones joined the Suns for the [[2017 NBA Summer League]]. In November 2017, he had multiple assignments to the Northern Arizona Suns of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/assignments/|title=2017–18 NBA Assignments|publisher=National Basketball Association|access-date=December 7, 2017}} On December 7, 2017, he was waived by the Suns.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/suns-sign-mike-james-standard-nba-contract|title=Suns Sign Mike James to Standard NBA Contract|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=December 7, 2017|access-date=December 7, 2017}} Jones appeared in 38 games with Phoenix over two seasons, averaging 4.7 points and 2.2 rebounds in 15.2 minutes. On December 12, 2017, Jones was acquired by the [[Northern Arizona Suns]],{{cite web|url=http://northernarizona.gleague.nba.com/news/naz-suns-acquire-forward-derrick-jones-jr/|title=NAZ Suns Acquire Forward Derrick Jones Jr.|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=December 12, 2017|access-date=December 19, 2017}} but did not appear in any games before signing with the Miami Heat later that month. ===Miami Heat (2017–2020)=== On December 31, 2017, Jones signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/heat-signs-derrick-jones-jr|title=HEAT Signs Derrick Jones Jr.|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=December 31, 2017|access-date=December 31, 2017}} On a two-way contract, Jones split his playing time between the Heat and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]]. He made his first start for the Heat on January 9, 2018, in just his third game, recording eight points, five rebounds, one assist and two blocks in 28 minutes against the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/j/jonesde02/gamelog/2018/|title=Derrick Jones 2017–18 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=March 6, 2018}} On July 1, 2018, Jones signed a 2-year, $3.2 million standard contract with the Heat.{{Cite web |title=2018 NBA free agency grades: Heat bringing back Derrick Jones Jr. |url=https://hoopshabit.com/2018/07/02/2018-nba-free-agency-grades-heat-bringing-back-derrick-jones-jr/ |access-date=March 12, 2022 |website=Fansided}} Jones won the [[Slam Dunk Contest]] over [[Aaron Gordon]] during the [[2020 NBA All-Star Weekend]]. They both had perfect scores in their first two dunks in the second round, forcing an overtime round. After they both earned perfect scores on their initial dunks, Jones won by scoring a 48 after taking off just past the free throw line to complete a windmill dunk; Gordon received a 47 after dunking over {{convert|7|ft|6|in|adj=on}} [[Tacko Fall]].{{cite news|last=Chiang|first=Anthony|title=All-Star Saturday turned into the Heat's night. Inside big nights for Jones Jr. and Adebayo|date=February 16, 2020|newspaper=Miami Herald|url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/nba/miami-heat/article240345826.html|access-date=February 16, 2020}} On August 14, 2020, Jones Jr. suffered a neck strain after colliding with Indiana center Goga Bitadze. He was stretchered off the court. The Heat reached the [[2020 NBA Finals]], but lost in 6 games to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{Cite web |title=The Finals Stat, Game 6: Lakers dominate at the rim |url=https://www.nba.com/news/finals-stat-lakers-heat-6 |access-date=February 20, 2024 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} ===Portland Trail Blazers (2020–2021)=== On November 22, 2020, Jones signed a 2-year, $19 million contract with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/2020/11/22/blazers-sign-derrick-jones-jr|title=TRAIL BLAZERS SIGN DERRICK JONES JR|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=November 22, 2020}}{{Cite web |title=Trail Blazers Rumors: Derrick Jones Jr. Agrees to 2-Year, $19M Contract |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2893488-trail-blazers-rumors-derrick-jones-jr-agrees-to-2-year-19m-contract |access-date=March 12, 2022 |website=Bleacher Report}} ===Chicago Bulls (2021–2023)=== On August 28, 2021, Jones was acquired, alongside a first and a second round pick, by the [[Chicago Bulls]] in a three-team sign-and-trade also involving the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web|title=BULLS ACQUIRE DERRICK JONES JR. IN THREE-TEAM TRADE WITH PORTLAND AND CLEVELAND|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-acquire-derrick-jones-jr-three-team-trade-portland-and-cleveland|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=August 28, 2021|access-date=August 29, 2021}} On January 12, 2022, during a 112–138 loss to the [[Brooklyn Nets]], he suffered a right knee injury. The next day, the Bulls announced that he had a [[bone bruise]] and would miss at least 4-to-6 weeks, although the timetable was later upgraded to 2-to-4 weeks.{{cite web|title=Bulls say Derrick Jones Jr. (knee) is expected to miss 2–4 weeks|url=https://www.nba.com/news/report-bulls-derrick-jones-jr-knee-out-4-6-weeks|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=January 13, 2022|access-date=March 23, 2022}} On January 25, the Bulls announced that Jones had fractured his right index finger during a workout and would miss an additional 6-to-8 weeks.{{cite web|first=Paul|last=Kasabian|title=Bulls' Derrick Jones Jr. Out 6–8 Weeks; Finger Injury Diagnosed as Fracture|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10024974-bulls-derrick-jones-jr-out-6-8-weeks-finger-injury-diagnosed-as-fracture|website=BleacherReport.com|date=January 26, 2022|access-date=March 23, 2022}} On the same day, however, he was upgraded to a timetable of 1-to-2 weeks in order to determine if he could play with a [[Splint (medicine)|splint]].{{cite web|title=Bulls' Derrick Jones: Will be re-evaluated in 1–2 weeks|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/bulls-derrick-jones-will-be-re-evaluated-in-1-2-weeks/|website=CBSSports.com|date=January 26, 2022|access-date=March 23, 2022}} On July 6, 2022, Jones re-signed with the Bulls on a two-year, $6.6 million contract.{{cite web|title=Bulls Sign Drummond and Jones Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-drummond-and-jones-jr|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=July 6, 2022|access-date=July 6, 2022}}{{cite web|first=Larry|last=Hawley|title=Report: Derrick Jones Jr., Bulls agree on new contract|url=https://wgntv.com/sports/bulls/report-derrick-jones-jr-bulls-agree-on-new-contract/|website=WGNTV.com|date=July 1, 2022|access-date=July 9, 2022}} On June 21, 2023, Jones declined his $3.36 million player option to become a free agent.{{cite web|first=Ryan|last=Taylor|title=Report: Bulls forward Derrick Jones Jr. declines player option for 2023–24 season|url=https://www.nbcsportschicago.com/nba/chicago-bulls/bulls-news/report-bulls-forward-derrick-jones-jr-declines-player-option-for-2023-24-season/490796/?amp=1|website=NBCSportsChicago.com|date=June 21, 2023|access-date=June 21, 2023}} ===Dallas Mavericks (2023–2024)=== On August 18, 2023, Jones signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{Cite web |title=Mavericks sign former Slam Dunk champ Derrick Jones Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/news/mavericks-sign-derrick-jones-jr|date=August 18, 2023|access-date=August 18, 2023|website=nba.com}} He made his debut for the Mavericks on October 25, 2023, in a 126–119 win over the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401584701|title=Mavericks spoil Victor Wembanyama's NBA debut, beat the Spurs 126–119 in the teams' opener|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=October 25, 2023|access-date=October 25, 2023}} Jones' time with the Mavericks marked a significant chapter in his career. Although initially coming off the bench, he earned a spot in the starting lineup later in the season due to his elite defensive play and impact on the court. During the playoffs, Jones' defense, athleticism and hustle were instrumental in several critical games, where his shot-blocking, perimeter defense and rebounding helped the Mavericks reach the [[2024 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]]. During this run, he primarily guarded the opposing team's best player, including [[Paul George]], [[Shai Gilgeous-Alexander]], and [[Anthony Edwards (basketball)|Anthony Edwards]]. Jones continued to improve his offensive game as well, showing flashes of increased confidence with his outside shot and becoming a reliable cutter to the basket. His presence helped solidify the Mavericks' rotation, and this season is considered the most impactful stretch of his NBA career. He helped the Mavericks reach the [[2024 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]], but they lost to the [[Boston Celtics]] in five games.{{cite web|title=Boston Celtics defeat Dallas Mavericks to win 2024 NBA Finals|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/boston-celtics-beat-dallas-mavericks-2024-nba-finals/|publisher=cbsnews.com|access-date=June 17, 2024|date=June 17, 2024}} ===Los Angeles Clippers (2024–present)=== On July 10, 2024, Jones signed a three-year, $30 million contract with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|title=LA Clippers Sign Derrick Jones Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/la-clippers-sign-derrick-jones-jr|website=NBA.com|date=July 10, 2024|access-date=July 10, 2024}} He made 77 appearances (55 starts) for Los Angeles during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 10.1 points, 3.4 rebounds, and 0.8 assists. On November 17, 2025, Jones was ruled out for at least six weeks after being diagnosed with a sprained [[medial collateral ligament|MCL]] in his right knee.{{Cite web|title=Sources: Clippers' Derrick Jones Jr. (MCL) out at least 6 weeks|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/47002971/sources-clippers-derrick-jones-jr-mcl-least-6-weeks|access-date=January 19, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} Upon returning from injury, he made four appearances off of the bench, having previously started the first 13 games of the season. On January 4, 2026, Jones was ruled out for another six weeks after being diagnosed with a Grade 2 MCL sprained in the same knee.{{Cite web|title=Sources: Clippers' Jones Jr. out with another MCL sprain|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/47507092/sources-clippers-jones-jr-another-mcl-sprain|access-date=January 19, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player
